name: fix-worktrees
contract:
# Contract: release fixes, part C: managed worktrees and setup

## Goal

foreman's first release is blocked on findings from three architecture reviews. This unit fixes worktree creation, setup and rollback: C1, C8, C9 and B3.

- C1: rollback must never remove a worktree or branch foreman can't prove it created in that call. Track ownership of the branch and of the worktree separately; validate identity (path, branch, and that it's the worktree foreman added) before any removal; never `--force` a removal of a worktree with changes; delete branches by expected OID.
- C8: setup gets a deadline (a sensible default, configurable per start with a flag if the CLI needs one; say what you chose) and a cancellation path; on timeout or cancellation, terminate and join the process group, roll back safely, and release the reservation.
- C9: bound what the process helper keeps from a command's output (a tail buffer), with an explicit limit and a visible overflow note for callers that need complete output.
- B3: the daemon enforces Start's mode constraints itself (`setup` and `from` only with `newWorktree`; `newWorktree` and `worktree` exclusive) before any side effect, in a shared validator the CLI uses too.

## Scope

- May change: `src/core/managed-worktree.ts`, `src/core/process.ts`, `src/core/preflight/`, `src/supervisor/turns.ts` (Start's validation and setup sequence only), a new shared validator under `src/core/` or `src/schemas/`, `src/commands/runs.ts` (start flags only), `tests/` for these (new `tests/managed-worktree*.test.ts`, `tests/process*.test.ts`, and Start cases in `tests/supervisor-integration.test.ts`), `docs/rfcs/0001-foreman.md` (the managed worktree section).
- Owned by other units: the rest of `src/supervisor/`, `src/daemon/`, `src/core/runs/`, `src/core/doctor.ts`, `src/core/command-output.ts`, `src/core/commands.ts`, `src/schemas/codex.ts`, `README.md`, `npm/`, `.github/`.

## How to work

The findings are in `/tmp/scratch` (outside the repo; read it, don't copy it into a tracked file). Each finding has a location, a failure scenario and a proposed fix. The reviewers read the code carefully but could be wrong: confirm each finding against the code before fixing it, and if one is wrong, say so with evidence in the hand-off instead of changing code. If a proposed fix isn't the simplest conventional one, use the better fix and say why.

Read first, in this repo: `AGENTS.md` (all of it, especially Testing and Error handling), `README.md`, `docs/rfcs/0001-foreman.md`, the repo rules (`.claude/rules/effect.md`, `.claude/rules/src/cli.md`, `.claude/rules/src/effect-services.md`, `.claude/rules/src/typescript.md`, `.claude/rules/src/testing.md`, `.claude/rules/src/verification.md`) and the docs each one links, and `docs/guidance/effect/api.md`.

Three other delegates fix other findings in parallel from the same `main` commit, each owning different files (see Scope). Stay inside yours; where a finding needs a file another unit owns, do your side, describe the other side precisely in the hand-off, and the orchestrator will reconcile at merge. Don't ask about this through `ask_orchestrator` unless you're actually blocked.

## Acceptance

Real services, processes, sockets and git repos with the fake app server; no real inference in `tests/` or `e2e/` (AGENTS.md "Testing"). Every finding you fix starts with a test that fails before the fix and passes after, revert-verified; concurrency findings need tests that force the interleaving deterministically (barriers, `TestClock`, fault injection), never sleeps. Run each new or changed test file at least three times, `bun run lint`, `bun run typecheck`, `bun run e2e`, and `bun run test` once at the end; report the counts. Don't run `bun run check`. If your area has a real-Codex path, run `FOREMAN_SMOKE=1 FOREMAN_SMOKE_SHORT=1 bun run smoke` once after building (a development check; credits are not a concern).

QA as the first user of what you changed, with the built binary and a temporary `FOREMAN_HOME`, reproducing each blocker's failure scenario before and after where you can. Fix the friction you find (a bug gets a regression test first).

## Do not

- commit or push (leave the changes for review)
- disable a lint rule, weaken a test or add a cast to get green; split an over-complex function into named steps instead
- add features, options, abstractions or mechanisms the findings don't need
- remove any worktree, branch or run data that could hold work, in code or in tests outside temp directories
- add real-Codex tests anywhere `bun run check`, git hooks or CI would run them
- edit `~/.codex` config, hooks, trust or auth, or touch the real `~/.foreman`
- use `ask_orchestrator` for progress reports; use it only when blocked or when a decision is needed
- mention any repository outside this one in a tracked file

## Skills to apply

The `ce` skills and agents come from the Claude Code `claude-essentials` marketplace. Find the newest installed copy with:

```bash
ce=$(ls -d "$HOME"/.claude/plugins/cache/*/ce/*/ | sort -V | tail -1)
```

Read each skill that applies and use it on this task; your hand-off says where it changed what you did.

- `${ce}skills/writing-tests/SKILL.md`: for every test you write, before writing any. Where it and the repo's own testing rules differ, the repo wins. Also read its `references/waiting-typescript.md` for any test that waits on a process, socket, timer or file, and `references/flaky-tests.md` before you call a test done: run each new test file at least three times, and once in the full suite, since this repo has had tests that pass alone and fail under load. The hand-off's Checks section says which tests you wrote, what behaviour each pins down, and which failed before the fix.
- `${ce}skills/architecting-systems/SKILL.md`, with its `references/structure.md`, `coupling.md`, `boundaries.md` and `concurrency.md`: before adding a module.
- `${ce}skills/handling-errors/SKILL.md`: for any error handling you add.
- `${ce}skills/effect/SKILL.md`: for all Effect code.
- `.claude/skills/effect-development/SKILL.md` in this repo.

## Review before hand-off

Once the acceptance checks pass, get one independent code review and fix what it finds. The reviewer is the `ce:code-reviewer` agent (`${ce}agents/code-reviewer.md`) extended by the repo's `.claude/agents/code-reviewer.md` when it exists. This repo's command guard refuses compound shell commands, so run the review as separate simple commands:

1. `mktemp -d` and note the directory it prints, below `<review>`.
2. Write `<review>/prompt.md` with your file-writing tool (not a shell heredoc), containing: the `ce:code-reviewer` agent body without its frontmatter; the repo reviewer's body if that file exists; then these lines: "Skills: <ce>skills/architecting-systems/SKILL.md, <ce>skills/writing-tests/SKILL.md, <ce>skills/handling-errors/SKILL.md. The base branch is main; review the uncommitted work in <worktree>. Your sandbox is read-only, so don't run the tests; the author already ran the checks. The task's contract:" followed by this contract's text, from `/tmp/scratch`.
3. `codex exec --ephemeral --sandbox read-only -m gpt-sol -c model_reasoning_effort=high -c service_tier=priority -o <review>/review.md - < <review>/prompt.md`

Fix every finding in `review.md`, or say in the hand-off why a finding is wrong. A finding that is a bug gets a regression test in the repo before its fix, revert-verified. Then rerun the acceptance checks. One review pass only.

## Hand-off

You're done when the review's findings are resolved and the acceptance checks pass, or when you're blocked. Leave everything uncommitted and end with this report as your final message; the orchestrator works from it, so be specific and name files and symbols.

1. Summary: what you built, in two or three sentences.
2. Files: each file created or changed, with one line on why.
3. Decisions: choices the contract left open and why you made them; any deviation from the design or contract and the reason; where the skills changed your approach. Name every new mechanism you added and the acceptance test or contract line that needed it.
4. Checks: each command you ran and its result (test counts, not just "passed"), and the QA: what you ran, what you judged and what you changed.
5. Review: the review file's path, each finding in a line, and how you resolved it (fixed, or why not).
6. Look closer at: the places most likely to be wrong.
7. Open: what's left undone or blocked, and the questions you'd ask.

## 1. Summary

Implemented safe rollback, bounded process output, setup deadlines and cancellation, and daemon Start-mode validation. Both independent-review findings are fixed, and final checks pass. Changes remain uncommitted; two integrations in other units’ files remain under Open.

## 2. Files

- `src/core/managed-worktree.ts`: separate ownership tracking, identity checks, expected-OID deletion, safe receipt transfer, setup deadline and rollback diagnostics.
- `src/core/process.ts`: bounded output tails and visible overflow failures.
- `src/core/start-mode.ts`: new shared mode validator.
- `src/supervisor/turns.ts`: early validation, cancellable preflight and cancellation-outcome tracking.
- `src/commands/runs.ts`: Start budget help text.
- `tests/managed-worktree.test.ts`: six ownership, retention and concurrent-commit cases.
- `tests/process.test.ts`: complete-output overflow and bounded tail cases.
- `tests/supervisor-integration.test.ts`: eight Start/setup/cancellation cases.
- `docs/rfcs/0001-foreman.md`: managed-worktree behavior and limits.

## 3. Decisions

- Setup defaults to **10 minutes**. An explicit `start --budget` also sets its setup deadline; the turn receives a separate budget of that duration. No new flag or wire field.
- Rollback requires the original directory, `.git` file and administration-directory identities, expected branch and unchanged HEAD. Removal never uses `--force`; branch deletion uses the original expected OID.
- `createWorktree` transfers its ownership receipt before leaving its interruption mask. This addresses review finding 1.
- Preflight cancellation uses cancel/completion deferreds and records which outcome won. `cancelStart` acknowledges only a cancellation that won, after cleanup and reservation release.
- Complete output defaults to **1 MiB per stream**, with overflow failure. Setup requests **4096-byte tails per stream**, with an overflow note.
- Testing skills drove real temporary repos/processes, FIFO barriers and TestClock. Effect and error-handling skills drove scoped process cleanup and preservation of original failures alongside rollback failures. Architecture guidance kept the shared validator small.

## 4. Checks

|---|---|
| `bun run test:unit tests/process.test.ts tests/managed-worktree.test.ts tests/supervisor-integration.test.ts` | Final versions passed **three consecutive runs: 161 tests each** |

| `git diff --check` | Passed |
| `FOREMAN_SMOKE=1 FOREMAN_SMOKE_SHORT=1 bun run smoke` | Final: **16 passed, 0 failed** |

All four findings were reproduced and revert-verified: restoring the original implementation caused **13 selected failures**. Reverting the review fixes and diagnostic correction caused **3 selected failures**.

The tests pin foreign-worktree preservation, dirty/committed/replaced-worktree retention, expected-OID deletion, bounded output, raw socket validation, default/custom setup deadlines, process-group cleanup, reservation reuse and cancellation correctness.

Built-binary QA reproduced the original failures and confirmed the fixes:

- Invalid socket setup modified main originally; fixed Start left it untouched.
- The original rollback deleted foreign work; the fixed rollback preserved it.
- Original setup hung beyond its requested budget; fixed setup timed out and allowed daemon shutdown.
- Verbose setup now retains its tail and reports overflow.

Earlier failures resolved during development included output-shape compatibility, formatting and type errors. Two intermittent cases remain relevant to the orchestrator: an existing recovery/wait test failed once in ten isolated runs, then passed nine times; the first smoke run had a proxy `EPIPE` failure, which passed individually and in the final full smoke run.

## 5. Review

Review: [review.md](/tmp/foreman-worktree-review.Sun8U9/review.md).

1. Lost ownership receipt during cancellation: **fixed** by transferring it inside the creation mask; regression and revert-verified.
2. False cancellation acknowledgement after preflight wins: **fixed** by returning the recorded cancellation outcome; regression and revert-verified.

One independent review pass was performed.

## 6. Look closer at

- `createWorktree`, `removeCreatedWorktree` and the filesystem identity comparisons.
- The choice to reuse explicit `start --budget` for setup.
- Compatibility between the new complete-output limit and other units’ command callers.

## 7. Open

Required merge wiring, left untouched because those files belong to other units:

1. **`src/supervisor/index.ts`**: Interrupt dispatch must call `turns.cancelStart(body.name)` **before lookup or taking the run/name lock**. Return `Ok` when it returns true; otherwise continue through normal registered-run interruption.
2. **`src/core/commands.ts`**: replace Start’s existing inline mode predicate with `yield* validateStartMode(input)`. The CLI currently retains its original validation; the daemon uses the shared helper.
3. **`README.md`**: document the ten-minute setup default and explicit budget behavior.

The existing recovery/wait intermittency is consistent with the separately assigned state/event publication finding. Its diagnostic log is [recovery-repeat.log](/tmp/foreman-worktree-qa.qBFiBF/recovery-repeat.log). No design questions remain.
